articles.description:
It's a Swedish musical takeover! Or do we call it a smorgasbord? 
Look for Tiny Desk Radio on your local NPR station.
articles.title: Tiny Desk Radio: First Aid Kit, Snoh Aalegra, Robyn

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market.
articles.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year

articles.author: Scott Detrow
articles.description: The stock market is ending the week down despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO and a strong Nvidia earnings report, largely thanks to investor jitters about the future of AI.
articles.title: Tech stocks end the week on a down note, despite Anthropic's mega-IPO

articles.author: Debbie Elliott
articles.description: The only known handwritten draft of The Reverend Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech is on display in his hometown. The iconic phrase, however, never made it on the page.
articles.title: MLK's handwritten draft of iconic speech on display for the first time

articles.author: Rachel Treisman
articles.description: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.
articles.title: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court

articles.author: Trevor Smith
articles.description: Sage Bava grew up on a nature preserve in New York. Julieta Eugenio found inspiration on daily walks through Brooklyn's Prospect Park. Both musicians talk about how nature inspired their sound.
articles.title: How two musicians found inspiration among the trees

articles.author: Miles Parks
articles.description: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.
articles.title: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair

articles.author: Candice Lim
articles.description: This prequel tells the origin story of Haymitch Abernathy.
articles.title: 'Sunrise on the Reaping' feels like sunset for the 'Hunger Games' franchise

articles.author: Nia Dumas
articles.description: Orchestra Noir is back on tour, selling out stages across the country and proving classical music can be anything you want it to be.
articles.title: How Orchestra Noir turned classical music into a cultural movement

articles.author: Franco Ordoñez
articles.description: At a White House press conference Friday, Trump offered little in actual results of the meetings, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues.
articles.title: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers little results

articles.author: Emine Sinmaz and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
Experts say no law states third-party consent is a valid defence and call for public debate and further education 
Campaigners have welcomed a call for scrutiny of consent laws by a survivor of drug-facilitated rape but said action must also focus on wider issues around sexual assault.
Joanne Young, who was drugged and raped by her husband and sexually abused by men he invited into their home, warned of “serious questions about how the law deals with consent”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Campaigners back call for scrutiny of consent laws by Joanne Young

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv; photographs by Julia Kochetova
articles.description:
Despite dodging tears in the tarmac, people are confident in city’s infrastructure – and will not worry about what has not happened yet
Mykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20 to 24 times a day past the holes in the road on Kyiv’s damaged Northern Bridge that were caused by a Russian ballistic missile attack on Tuesday.
Buses are now the only motor transport allowed across the normally busy multi-lane crossing, though on their way into the city centre they have to skirt the tears in the tarmac, using the only functioning lane to get by.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
articles.description:
Charity that collects the coins says donations are down by £200,000 after a barrier was put in place to restrict access
When Jeff Clinton, an American visiting Rome with his wife for the first time, found a US one-cent coin on a street close to Termini train station, he knew precisely what he was going to do with it. “I’ll throw it into the Trevi fountain,” said Clinton, holding the copper coin in the palm of his hand as the couple admired the landmark.
He was well aware of the tradition among tourists of tossing a coin over their shoulder and into the waters of the baroque masterpiece, in a ritual fabled to ensure a return visit to the city or make other dreams come true.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tourists are throwing fewer coins into Rome’s Trevi fountain – is €2 entry fee to blame?

articles.author: Nino Bucci
articles.description:
Victoria police say boy, 17, communicated with offenders under username ‘Onepercent’

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victorian police allege a 17-year-old boy tasked others to carry out a series of arsons, home invasions and a mistaken identity kidnapping that resulted in the partial amputation of a victim’s finger during Melbourne’s hospitality wars.
The boy, who was arrested on Friday afternoon, allegedly communicated with the offenders under the username “Onepercent” on the encrypted communications app Signal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Teenager allegedly organised arsons and kidnapping on Signal during Melbourne hospitality wars

articles.author: Kaamil Ahmed
articles.description:
Survivors recount rivers red with blood and burning nearby villages serving as an urgent warning to flee their homes
Smoke was often the signal to run – seen from a distance, it was the indication for Rohingya that a neighbouring village was under attack and that theirs would be next.
In other places, they saw the rivers run red and would pull out the bodies, perform quick burial rites and then flee.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rohingya who escaped Myanmar’s genocide tell their stories

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time
Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games has announced, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.
The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar said also it had sold 32.5m units of the game on prerelease, setting a record across platforms.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A new record for entertainment’: Grand Theft Auto VI sales hit $3.8bn on first day of release, developer says

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury
The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that came months after his first trial concluded with a hung jury.
For two weeks, a fresh batch of jurors listened to prosecutors mount their case against Jonathan Rinderknecht.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty

articles.author: Henry Belot
articles.description:
Exclusive: Independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s cards instruct people to vote in a way that would benefit Liberal party

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Greens are seeking an urgent injunction from the supreme court to stop an independent candidate distributing how-to-vote cards that allegedly mimic the party’s branding and urge people to preference it last.
As prepoll opened on Wednesday morning, Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s campaign team handed out how-to-vote cards that used the minor party’s colour scheme, font and triangle logo with the banner “Vote 1 Green Values”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Victorian Greens seek urgent injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight
“Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”
The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump turns White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition

articles.author: Maria G Ortiz-Briones
articles.description:
A public vigil and celebration of life honor the civil rights activist and co-founder of United Farm Workers union
Hundreds of people came out to honor and celebrate the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta at a celebration-of-life event Friday in Bakersfield.
Huerta’s daughter Lori de Leon thanked attendees for their support during her mother’s passing, highlighting the widespread tributes and communities gathering in her honor.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A source of inspiration’: California celebrates the late civil rights icon Dolores Huerta

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’ 
Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.
Tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Senate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial

articles.author: Penry Buckley and Lisa Cox
articles.description:
Labor says allowing mine to increase production reflects ‘gravity of situation facing hundreds of workers’ – but critics call it ‘unprecedented and dangerous’

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales government has passed special legislation to allow a coalmine in the Hunter Valley to increase production by 32% in its final act of parliament before the March state election, in which the region will be a key battleground for One Nation.
After a marathon session in the legislative council on Friday, the Minns government and the Coalition voted at 1.36am on Saturday morning to allow the Mount Pleasant mine to increase its annual extraction rate from 12.5MT to 16.5MT until 2032.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NSW passes Mount Pleasant coalmine law as Greens claim change an attempt to head off One Nation

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Beating of Michel Zecler in 2020 sparked outrage over police brutality after it was caught on security cameras
Three French police officers who beat a black music producer they said was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic have been found guilty of intentional, racist violence.
The brutal assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, was caught on security cameras in his building in 2020 and triggered outrage in France over police brutality. The trial this month was considered a turning point for the recognition of racist violence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: French police officers found guilty of racist assault on black music producer

articles.author: Ben Doherty
articles.description:
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi
Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.
In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad

articles.author: Lauren Almeida and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout

Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.
Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading

articles.author: Alex Daniel
articles.description:
Jamie Dimon says he is ‘setting an example’ in seeking to claw back Labour’s increase in surcharge, from 3% to 6%
Jamie Dimon, the chief executive of JP Morgan, has said he will find ways to offset the chancellor’s tax rise for banks, calling the increase unfair.
Speaking at an event in London on Thursday, Dimon said he would seek to claw back the increase and was “setting an example so that [governments] understand the trade-offs of these unfair penalties”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: JP Morgan boss says he will find ways to offset ‘unfair’ rise in UK tax on banks

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Sally-Anne Bowen was found guilty of having sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the 1980s
A chemistry teacher who had sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the late 1980s has been arrested by police in Hampshire after she failed to turn up to her sentencing hearing.
Sally-Anne Bowen, 65, could not be found at her home by Metropolitan police officers on Friday morning after a warrant was issued for her arrest, a court heard.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police arrest teacher who missed sentencing after indecent assault conviction

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Dwain Hall was convicted of stabbing Sonia Exelby, a music teacher who prosecutors say suffered from mental illness
A Florida mechanic has been found guilty of stabbing to death a British music teacher, whom he convinced to travel to the United States.
Dwain Hall, an auto repair and tow truck driver, groomed 32-year-old Sonia Exelby from Portsmouth, England, on a fetish website before luring her to the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Florida mechanic found guilty of murdering British woman who attorney says came to US to die

articles.author: Timothy Pratt
articles.description:
Pro-Palestinian donor James ‘Fergie’ Chambers released as court considers extradition request
In a blur of events surrounding the Trump administration’s effort to extradite James “Fergie” Chambers, Spain released the wealthy US activist and donor on bail even as Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner, Stella Schnabel, acting on a request from US authorities.
Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spain frees wealthy US-sought activist on bail as Irish police raid Dublin home

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Nikhil Gupta admitted to plotting with Indian government official to hire hitman to murder dual US-Canadian citizen
An Indian ⁠man was sentenced to more ⁠than 19 ​years in US prison on Friday after admitting to orchestrating a failed Indian government-backed plot to kill a Sikh separatist in New York ⁠City, in connection with what US and Canadian authorities have called a broader effort to target Indian dissidents.
Nikhil Gupta, 55, pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy ⁠to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 19 years in prison for conspiring to kill Sikh separatist in New York

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
PM challenges rivals to rebuff plan he says could add 0.5% annual growth to economy and offer young people hope
Several sentences into a slightly convoluted answer about where UK-EU relations might go next, Andy Burnham abruptly changed tack. “The important point is that the Britain of today and the EU of today is not the one of 2016,” he said. “Life has moved on in so many ways.”
This is undoubtedly true. But Burnham’s political gamble on closer ties with Brussels hinges on the assumption that most British voters feel this way as well.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Misty-eyed Burnham gambles on closer ties with EU as he throws down gauntlet to Tories and Reform

articles.author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
articles.description:
The pair had taken off from the Scottish Gliding Centre at nearby Portmoak on a training flight
Two men have been killed after their glider crashed into Loch Leven, a large body of water in Perth and Kinross, on Friday morning.
Police Scotland said their bodies were recovered from the loch by the emergency services after the alarm was raised at 11.05am on Friday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two men killed after glider crashes into Loch Leven in Scotland

articles.author: Anne Davies
articles.description:
The opposition’s struggle is creating an opportunity for progressive independents who are boosted by shrewd political operator Chris Minns

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales Coalition is facing a renewed threat to its heartland seats on Sydney’s north shore.
This time, the threat is from independent candidates – and they’re backed by the same community activists who put a swathe of teal independents into federal parliament.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: As the Coalition stares down One Nation in NSW, a new threat is rising: the teals

articles.author: Jason Burke
articles.description:
Reactions to ICJ ruling underline global divisions over court with China raising concerns about judicial overreach
The US has greeted with caution the world’s highest court’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, while China has raised concerns of judicial overreach.
Reactions to Thursday’s historic ruling underlined deep international division over the role of the court and similar institutions. The international court of justice (ICJ) had never previously found a state responsible for genocide and the decision could set a precedent for future genocide claims, notably a case against Israel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US reacts cautiously to Myanmar genocide ruling as EU praises ‘critical’ role of UN’s top court

articles.author: José Olivares
articles.description:
Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike
The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.”
A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Weak and dizzy’: the secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
State attorney says scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if company misled investors
California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.
Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California investigates Nvidia over whether chip exports ended up in China

articles.author: Alice Nightingale-Smith for MetDesk
articles.description:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded
Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.
Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state

articles.author: Catie McLeod
articles.description:
Testing confirms presence of etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three people who lost consciousness and were hospitalised in New South Wales after using certain vapes have tested positive for the unregulated anaesthetic agent etomidate, health officials said.
NSW health on Friday issued a public warning about vape liquids containing etomidate, a strong and fast-acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas but not registered for medical use in Australia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Vape users hospitalised after losing consciousness, prompting public health warning in New South Wales

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic Editor
articles.description:
Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner
The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.
Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers

articles.author: Ali Aziz, Maria Talal and Tom Levitt
articles.description:
Al-Qadisiyah University’s move a sign of the country’s slide into a Taliban-like gender segregation, say activists
The removal of male professors teaching female students at a university in southern Iraq has sparked protests and been criticised by activists as a Taliban-like gender segregation policy.
As many as 400 women are estimated to have joined protests over the past two weeks calling for the return of their professors at Al-Qadisiyah University in a move that appears to have surprised its administrators.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iraq university’s removal of male professors teaching women sparks weeks of protests

articles.author: Julian Borger
articles.description:
Hailed as ‘a rare moment of justice’, judges’ decision sets out a roadmap for assessing the question of intent
The international court of justice (ICJ) verdict making Myanmar the first country in history to be found guilty of committing genocide does not just deliver justice for Rohingya victims. It also gives the 1948 genocide convention new relevance in governing the actions of nation states.
In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Myanmar ruling gives new relevance to genocide convention and is ‘full of messages’ for Israel

articles.author: Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen
articles.description:
Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’

China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.
The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it said was the protection of diplomatic immunity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars

articles.author: Ariana Baio
articles.description:
US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake
Donald Trump was, again, accused of falling asleep during a televised event, this time during the speech of the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in China.
The US president appeared to close his eyes for roughly 10 seconds on Thursday. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump accused of falling asleep during Xi Jinping speech at Apec summit in China

articles.author: Kaamil Ahmed in The Hague and Yassin Abdumonab in Cox's Bazar
articles.description:
Relief in the immediate aftermath of a landmark ruling, but what happens next is in the hands of governments around the world
There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh as the scattered communities of Rohingya watched the UN’s top court rule the Myanmar military had committed genocide against them.
For almost a decade, the Rohingya have awaited this moment; recognition from the international court of justice (ICJ) that Myanmar in 2017 intentionally tried to destroy the mostly Muslim minority group through a campaign of mass killings and rape. More than 10,000 Rohingya were killed and 700,000 fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Everyone struggled for this justice’: tears in court as Rohingya vindicated in Myanmar genocide ruling

articles.author: Kaamil Ahmed in The Hague, and Oliver Holmes
articles.description:
Judgment finds ‘intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population’ after case seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of state crimes
Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 military campaign, the world’s highest court has ruled, in a historic and unprecedented decision.
The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle that was seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
articles.description:
First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu
The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.
Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage shows driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim
Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel.
Footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away. Three of those injured were in moderate condition, and several of the victims were women leaving a nearby wedding, the Times of Israel reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Eight injured after driver in Israel repeatedly rams car into Palestinians

articles.author: Rebecca Ratcliffe
articles.description:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits
Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked

articles.author: Sarah Johnson
articles.description:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds
One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse
A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.
Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president

articles.author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
articles.description:
Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago
Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.
Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu
Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.
Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever new administration was formed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza
Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.
The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans
The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.
The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt

articles.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
articles.description:
St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access
The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.
On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight
“Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”
The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump turns White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now);Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell, Tom Ambrose and Fran Singh (earlier)
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

We’re also following the latest on Capitol Hill as the battle for Senate majority leader between Democrats Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen plays out.
We had a key update on Wednesday, when Elissa Slotkin, the influential senator from Michigan, pledged her support for Van Hollen, a progressive. While Slotkin had been vocal that she would not back Schumer in the secret-ballot election on 1 December, saying that she wanted to see change in party leadership as Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers of Congress, until now she had not said whether Van Hollen had her vote.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican senator blocks Trump pick to lead cybersecurity agency who denied US Capitol was attacked on January 6 – as it happened

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’ 
Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.
Tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Senate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial

articles.author: Ben Doherty
articles.description:
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi
Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.
In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad

articles.author: Sophie Sullivan
articles.description:
Democrats – including incoming banking chair and both majority leader candidates – said wealthy interests were prioritized over the needs of working Americans
In response to a Guardian investigation, four US Senate Democrats say they will work to resurrect a financial watchdog agency that has abandoned dozens of enforcement actions under the second Trump administration.
The Guardian found that after the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) dropped more than 20 lawsuits against banks and corporations accused of a range of financial misconduct, complaints against those firms rose by an average of more than 75%. In many of these recent complaints, consumers described the same issues the CFPB’s suits had sought to address.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Worth fighting for’: senators vow to restore financial watchdog agency after Guardian investigation

articles.author: Dustin Guastella and Jared Abbott
articles.description:
Our analysis shows that ‘Bernie-Dog’ candidates are the most underrated success stories in US politics
Democrats had a huge night on 3 November. The party ran an average of about 15 points ahead of Kamala Harris’s 2024 margins, and picked up seats that Trump carried by double digits just two years ago.
Of course, the size and scope of the blue wave make it hard to draw specific lessons, and the results will inevitably serve as a Rorschach test reflecting each commentator’s prior beliefs. Democrats of all stripes won elections in all sorts of unlikely places.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: If Democrats want to win, blue-collar populists are the key | Dustin Guastella and Jared Abbott

articles.author: Hilary Beaumont with photographs by Simon Simard
articles.description:
Despite the president’s attacks, Sea Services is training New England fishers in offshore wind construction and providing them with a second income stream
On a rainy September morning, the Pamela Ann, a rusty, 86ft (26-metre) scallop boat, docked in New Bedford, Massachusetts. Its crew had spent the past 12 days at sea, recording mammal sightings, monitoring vessels to ensure they didn’t enter construction zones, and keeping watch over workers at Revolution Wind, a 65-turbine offshore wind project just south of Rhode Island.
“God forbid, if anybody was to fall, we could be there to help them out,” said Capt Kevin Souza, who has a bulldog tattoo on his shin to mark his time in the navy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: These US fishers see offshore wind as a ‘godsend’. Trump wants to shut it down

articles.author: Dana R Fisher
articles.description:
Political participation – in meetings, boycotts and demonstrations – has increased since Trump took office. It’s time for change
Over the past two years, Americans have watched as the Trump administration enacted Project 2025 and the US has descended into a state of lawless authoritarianism. Instead of sinking into a state of paralysis, though, Americans rose up to push back against the attacks, including limitations of voting rights and manipulations of political power through the gerrymandering of congressional districts.
Donald Trump’s actions motivated resistance in the streets in the form of large-scale public demonstrations, along with more localized mobilizations against ICE and the occupation of American cities. On 3 November, the collective response manifested as resistance at the ballot box.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump inspired a blue revolution. Can Democrats meet the moment? | Dana R Fisher

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland , produced by Danielle Stephens and Nada Smiljanic
articles.description:
Democrats who might be thinking of launching a presidential run in 2028 are starting to make moves. One such contender is Pete Buttigieg, the former transportation secretary under Joe Biden. Is he the candidate who can unite the broad church in his party?
There’s also talk that a vote to elect the new Senate leader could be moved up, helping Chuck Schumer retain power, after Chris Van Hollen challenged him for the position.
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Marianna Sotomayor of Puck News about the Democrats looking to shore up power on Capitol Hill and potentially head for the White House
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Could Pete Buttigieg win the White House in 2028? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Samantha Grasso in Austin
articles.description:
For organizers who spent decades trying to mobilize voters against a Republican government, a blue Texas felt like a pipe dream
Democratic victories in Texas came down like a deluge on election night after decades of drought.
James Talarico defeated the Texas attorney general, Ken Paxton, to become the state’s first elected Democratic US senator in nearly 30 years. Gina Hinojosa will soon be Texas’s first-ever Latina governor and its first Democratic governor since 1995. Texas Democrats also flipped 20 state House seats, three seats on the state board of education, all four Texas supreme court seats and all three Texas court of criminal appeals seats up for election.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From Beto to ‘Blexas’: how Democrats flipped Texas during the midterm elections

articles.author: Presented by Ian Sample , with Jessica Glenza , produced by Ellie Sans and Joshan Chana , the executive producer was Ellie Bury
articles.description:
This week the US lost its measles elimination status, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the country after being eliminated for 26 years. To find out what this means in practical terms for citizens, Ian Sample hears from the Guardian US health reporter Jessica Glenza. She explains why it comes at an already difficult time for the health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, and his Make America Healthy Again movement, and what newly elected Democrats will be focusing on when it comes to health
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Measles is officially back in the USA. Will Maha pay the price? - video

articles.author: George Chidi in Atlanta
articles.description:
Jamie Davis falls just short as Democrats across south wonder whether blue wave could have been even bigger
Democrats are celebrating after, with Mary Peltola’s victory in Alaska, they have officially secured 56 Senate seats after the midterm elections. But Jamie Davis, who lost an incredibly close election for a Senate seat in Louisiana and could have made it 57, told the Guardian it “stings to come close”.
In Louisiana, which has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 2008, Davis lost to the Republican congresswoman Julia Letlow 49.1% to 50.9%. He was about 25,000 votes short in a state that cast about 1.5m votes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It stings to come close’: Louisiana Democrat’s narrow failure to make it 57 Senate seats

articles.author: Roque Planas
articles.description:
Supreme court greenlit federal government’s plan to rampage through national park, but with Texas now flipped, there will be more hurdles 
The Trump administration’s plans to build a “smart border wall” through a 500-mile stretch of Texas that includes the Big Bend national park recently got the green light from the supreme court. But those efforts are likely to slam into a big, blue wall.
Last week’s decision – the result of a continuing challenge to the administration’s decision to waive dozens of federal laws to speed wall construction in the Big Bend region – dealt a major blow to environmentalists and park enthusiasts, as well as locals who value the region’s remoteness, landowners who could see their properties devalued and businesses that rely on outdoor tourism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The ‘blue wave’ could foil the Trump administration’s Big Bend wall plans

articles.author: Steve Cohen and Michael Shank
articles.description:
Anti-democratic behaviors won’t disappear overnight. The new Congress – and all of us – must rise to the occasion
Americans just witnessed a blue tsunami in the midterm elections, with historic firsts across many US states: the country’s first female Black governor, first female Native American governor, first Muslim US senator, and more.
And while the voters’ repudiation of Donald Trump’s agenda is clear, as Democrats seize the majority of both chambers of Congress, the work to defend our institutions from further democratic backsliding won’t ease up overnight.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: After a blue wave, Trump will dig in his heels. We must be more vigilant than ever | Steve Cohen and Michael Shank

articles.author: Judith Levine
articles.description:
He is responsible for the health of the American people. On his watch, thousands have become seriously ill
At least 11 Americans have died of measles since January 2025 – the month before Robert F Kennedy Jr became secretary of Health and Human Services.
One of Friday’s victims was a child, in Wisconsin, where a baby died of measles the week before. Pennsylvania has not disclosed the age of the other person.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Measles has come raging back in the US. Robert F Kennedy Jr should be impeached | Judith Levine

articles.description:
The homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, defended his decision to take a government plane to attend a football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas on Saturday, while thousands of flights had been canceled and airspace was closed during the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop over the weekend
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mullin defends taking government plane to college football game amid nationwide grounding – video

articles.description:
Hung Cao, the acting US navy secretary, who faced lawmakers to be confirmed as the permanent top official, said during his confirmation hearing that the eight suicide attempts on board the USS Abraham Lincoln – which returned last month from a record-breaking deployment rife with mental health crises and concerns about living conditions – were actually “suicide mitigations”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Acting US navy secretary refers to eight suicide attempts as 'suicide mitigations' – video

articles.author: Emine Sinmaz and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
Experts say no law states third-party consent is a valid defence and call for public debate and further education 
Campaigners have welcomed a call for scrutiny of consent laws by a survivor of drug-facilitated rape but said action must also focus on wider issues around sexual assault.
Joanne Young, who was drugged and raped by her husband and sexually abused by men he invited into their home, warned of “serious questions about how the law deals with consent”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Campaigners back call for scrutiny of consent laws by Joanne Young

articles.author: Lauren Almeida and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout

Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.
Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading

articles.author: Alex Daniel
articles.description:
Jamie Dimon says he is ‘setting an example’ in seeking to claw back Labour’s increase in surcharge, from 3% to 6%
Jamie Dimon, the chief executive of JP Morgan, has said he will find ways to offset the chancellor’s tax rise for banks, calling the increase unfair.
Speaking at an event in London on Thursday, Dimon said he would seek to claw back the increase and was “setting an example so that [governments] understand the trade-offs of these unfair penalties”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: JP Morgan boss says he will find ways to offset ‘unfair’ rise in UK tax on banks

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Sally-Anne Bowen was found guilty of having sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the 1980s
A chemistry teacher who had sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the late 1980s has been arrested by police in Hampshire after she failed to turn up to her sentencing hearing.
Sally-Anne Bowen, 65, could not be found at her home by Metropolitan police officers on Friday morning after a warrant was issued for her arrest, a court heard.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police arrest teacher who missed sentencing after indecent assault conviction

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Dwain Hall was convicted of stabbing Sonia Exelby, a music teacher who prosecutors say suffered from mental illness
A Florida mechanic has been found guilty of stabbing to death a British music teacher, whom he convinced to travel to the United States.
Dwain Hall, an auto repair and tow truck driver, groomed 32-year-old Sonia Exelby from Portsmouth, England, on a fetish website before luring her to the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Florida mechanic found guilty of murdering British woman who attorney says came to US to die

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
PM challenges rivals to rebuff plan he says could add 0.5% annual growth to economy and offer young people hope
Several sentences into a slightly convoluted answer about where UK-EU relations might go next, Andy Burnham abruptly changed tack. “The important point is that the Britain of today and the EU of today is not the one of 2016,” he said. “Life has moved on in so many ways.”
This is undoubtedly true. But Burnham’s political gamble on closer ties with Brussels hinges on the assumption that most British voters feel this way as well.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Misty-eyed Burnham gambles on closer ties with EU as he throws down gauntlet to Tories and Reform

articles.author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
articles.description:
The pair had taken off from the Scottish Gliding Centre at nearby Portmoak on a training flight
Two men have been killed after their glider crashed into Loch Leven, a large body of water in Perth and Kinross, on Friday morning.
Police Scotland said their bodies were recovered from the loch by the emergency services after the alarm was raised at 11.05am on Friday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two men killed after glider crashes into Loch Leven in Scotland

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
The two sides have come to agreements on food and drink, emissions trading and the youth exchange scheme

Burnham has agreed EU reset deal with tuition fees issue unresolved, says No 10

After months of on-off negotiations, leaks and late nights, the EU and UK have agreed a 12-page statement setting out the next steps in their relationship. What exactly have they agreed?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What exactly is in the deal between the UK and the EU?

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Farage issues warning to potential rivals and says he will fight next election as leader if ‘still here and fit and healthy’
Nigel Farage has said he does not see another person who could do his job as leader of Reform UK, in a warning shot to potential rivals who might seek to replace him.
The Reform UK leader delivered a message that he was going nowhere despite his worries over his personal safety in the wake of the killing of the Reform politician Ann Widdecombe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No one else in Reform is suitable to lead the party, Nigel Farage says

articles.author: Kevin Rawlinson and Aisha Down
articles.description:
News of vulnerability comes after retailers in at least seven European countries hit by cyber-attacks
A secret government cybersecurity operation recently warded off the risk of a cyber-attack on fridges and freezers in UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums, it has emerged.
An attack would have been similar to those that have caused many millions of euros of damage in continental Europe in recent months. But, while many retailers have now been protected, researchers warned that many more could still be vulnerable.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK operation wards off risk of cyber-attack on supermarket fridges and freezers

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now) and Jakub Krupa (earlier)
articles.description:
President of European Council says EU ‘remains open to have the closest possible relationship’ with the UK
Senior correspondent
 

 

 Making today’s reset deal contingent on a further agreement on the level of tuition fees for EU citizens is designed to neutralise the leverage London gets in the next six months, EU sources have said.
 

 

 Senior diplomats had already confirmed this week that the EU would defer the deal on the level of tuition fees for another six months, a move designed to give the UK leverage in parallel negotiations to have the UK included in Made in Europe legislation designed to protect EU supply chains against China.
 

 

 But the move to make the food and drink deal also contingent on a tuition fees deal effectively seeks to neutralise the leverage the UK gets today.
 

 

 This is a serious chess game and shows the EU, again, is willing to speak very warmly about the UK but will play absolute hard ball when it comes to conceding any points to a former member state.
 

 

 It was the same point France was making last night insisting the UK could not have voting rights on legislation in relation to food and drink.
During his meeting with businesses in Brussels, PM Burnham said his EU deal would add up to 0.5% to the UK’s GDP.
“We’re pretty much there, and it’s a really good deal.”
“Treasury analysis out today is saying that now it’s clear up to 0.5% on GDP as a result of the deal. The single biggest growth intervention in this Parliament.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU wants ‘closest possible relationship’ with UK after agreeing Brexit reset deal – live

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Survey of more than 7,000 shows that people in hundreds of former leave areas now want to rejoin EU
Voters in four out of five UK parliamentary seats now back rejoining the EU, including hundreds of former leave areas, such as the prime minister’s constituency of Makerfield, according to polling.
The constituency-level modelling across Great Britain found that 512 seats now favoured rejoining, while 73 backed staying out, and 47 were too close to call, in a survey that will boost Andy Burnham’s case for opening the debate on returning to the EU.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Voters in four out of five UK parliamentary seats back rejoining EU

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Young’s abusers were convicted through suspect-centric prosecution, though much more needs to be done for victims
Hope can be found in the darkest of places. Joanne Young stood outside Winchester crown court on Thursday and said she was relieved – not just for herself and her family – but for women in the future.
Young, who was subjected to years of drugging and rape by her husband, who invited other men to assault her, waived her anonymity to speak out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Joanne Young’s faith in justice system is sign of real change, but courts are still catching up

articles.author: Peter Walker, Jennifer Rankin and Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
Discord between EU and UK on whether arrangements for food and drink, emissions trading and youth mobility scheme depend on settlement for students
The UK and EU have agreed a reset deal, Downing Street has said, although the level of tuition fees EU students will pay to study at UK universities remains unresolved.
“The deal is done – negotiations have concluded,” a No 10 statement said, less than an hour after the prime minister, Andy Burnham, arrived at the summit venue in Brussels, where he was greeted by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, and António Costa, the European Council president.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham has agreed EU reset deal with tuition fees issue unresolved, says No 10

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Relatives speak out as inquest jury finds Alice Webb’s death after filler entered her organs was accidental
The family of a woman who died after a botched Brazilian butt lift have called for laws against “cosmetic cowboys” to be introduced before more people lose their lives.
Speaking as an inquest jury concluded Alice Webb’s death was accidental, her family said they were astonished people were still having BBLs despite what had happened to her.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bring in ‘cosmetic cowboys’ law to avoid more deaths, says family of butt lift victim

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Three Choirs unveils First Release white wine after long, hot summer led to earliest harvest start in 50 years
Forget beaujolais nouveau: a Gloucestershire vineyard has uncorked its 2026 vintage, giving the first taste of this year’s long, hot summer – and an answer to France’s autumn tradition of opening young wine straight after harvest.
Three Choirs near Newent has unveiled its First Release white wine after the earliest harvest in its 50 years of producing wine.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Gloucestershire nouveau’: UK vineyard uncorks its 2026 answer to beaujolais

articles.author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
articles.description:
Warnings over exploitation risks come amid push for investigation into supported exempt accommodation sector
The home secretary has launched an attack on providers of housing for vulnerable residents in her Birmingham constituency, saying she “smells a rat” after warnings over spiralling costs and risks of exploitation.
A push for an independent investigation into the supported exempt accommodation (SEA) sector in Birmingham, one of the largest in the country, is under way.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mahmood ‘smells a rat’ over housing provision for vulnerable people in Birmingham

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Surge fuelled by ‘preppers’ heeding Be Ready campaign’s call for households to have three days of food and water for emergencies
Retail sales in Great Britain surged last month as the public rushed to buy products including tinned food and long-life milk, after the government issued a warning to stock up in case of a disaster.
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said the volume of goods sold jumped by 0.7% month on month in October, defying economists’ consensus expectations of flat sales, as “preppers” took heed of the government’s Be Ready campaign to hold supplies to last 72 hours to survive a possible extreme weather event, cyber incident or another serious emergency.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Household rush to stockpile emergency supplies sends British retail sales soaring

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Lifelong guardianship ceremonies were announced in July as way to publicly affirm chosen connections

Allan was 14 years old and had been through eight foster families and a stint in a children’s home when he began living with foster carer Russ in Kettering – a move that would change the course of his life.
Russ, 63, fought for Allan to get the school placements he needed and took him to kickboxing every week, eventually joining in himself. When Allan turned 18, he moved out into his own flat, but the pair have stayed close.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘You’ve got me for life’: first ceremonies in England cement care leavers’ relationships

articles.author: Hilary Osborne
articles.description:
From cashback on what you buy to cut-price gift cards, we offer tips on how to maximise savings on your shopping
With Black Friday on the horizon, retailers are already offering discounts, and over the next few weeks you can expect to see more price cuts as they attempt to entice us to open our wallets.
It could be a great time to snap up the things on your Christmas list or buy household items you need yourself. And there are ways to maximise your savings on Black Friday – which this year falls on 27 November – by doubling up on discounts, or earning cashback on your purchases.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How to get a bigger Black Friday bargain: cashback, price matches and gift cards

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing
A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades.
In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib, during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’

articles.author: Dalya Alberge
articles.description:
Exclusive: Guards told their jobs will be transferred to a private contractor that has rejected union recognition
The British Library has sparked outrage over plans to outsource its security workforce and hand over to a private company three of its public reading rooms, to be “repurposed” as business spaces for hire – despite having reportedly received millions of pounds from the public purse to refurbish those spaces.
Almost 70 guards have been told that their jobs will be transferred to a private contractor, STM, on 1 December. Their union, the PCS, has in turn been informed that STM has rejected union recognition for those staff.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Library to outsource security and ‘repurpose’ reading rooms as business spaces

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
As talks are held in Brussels over closer relations, we examine the economic context and the challenges ahead
The UK and EU will hold the second summit since Brexit on Friday against a volatile economic backdrop.
Taking place in Brussels as the war in the Middle East hits the global economy, the prime minister, Andy Burnham, will meet the head of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, and the president of the European Council, António Costa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What impact has Brexit had on the UK and EU economies?

articles.author: Matthew Weaver
articles.description:
Exclusive: Investigation launched after details of grief and trauma uploaded, raising questions over extent of issue
The Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) has launched an investigation after a patient was “horrified” to discover that notes of sensitive discussions with her psychotherapist had been shared through a system used by more than 100,000 NHS workers.
Rosanna (not her real name) found out that her detailed therapist’s notes, including about her grief and trauma, had been uploaded to her patient records when she saw them on a computer screen during a visit to her GP.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Patient ‘horrified’ to find her sensitive discussions were shared on system used by more than 100,000 NHS staff

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Polly Hudson, produced by Ruth Abrahams, Saskia Collette, Eleanor Biggs, Harriet Mogie and Brian McNamara; executive producer Homa Khaleeli
articles.description:
After Russell Brand’s conviction and accusations against David Walliams, campaigners are calling for a staggered age of consent. Nosheen Iqbal speaks to the columnist Polly Hudson and the educator Michael Conroy about what needs to change
Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com
Anger, disgust, shame. In the last couple of weeks, as news of famous older men being convicted and accused of crimes against very young women and girls has emerged, the public mood has shifted.
The conversation has moved from “how did society let this happen?” to “how do we stop it from happening again?”. In that space, a campaign has grown for the consent gap to be closed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is it time to change the UK age of consent? – podcast

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Hotly anticipated Bonnie and Clyde-inspired adventure GTA VI has gamers glued to their screens around the world
Grand Theft Auto fans around the world pulled all-nighters, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to vicariously embark on police chases and coordinate robberies as the latest instalment of the eagerly anticipated series arrived.
GTA VI, a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired crime adventure game set in the fictional US state of Leonida, was launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13-year wait.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters to play new instalment

articles.description:
After the conviction of four men for sexually assaulting and raping her at the invitation of her husband, Philip Young, Joanne Young – who waived her anonymity before the prosecution – read a statement outside Winchester crown court. In it, she reflected on her belief that the case held a wider message about how the law deals with consent, and what the prosecution might mean for other women who are the victims of abuse by men

Woman raped by strangers after being drugged by husband calls for consent law changes

Spiked nightcaps and invitations to strangers: how Philip Young sexually abused his wife for 15 years

 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Silence is not an option’: Joanne Young makes statement outside court – video

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Actors Mark Lewis Jones and Osian Morgan, who voiced characters in dub of 1977 film, among guests on red carpet
It has been a memorable few days for Wales. At the weekend, the men’s rugby team secured a historic win against New Zealand – their first victory over the All Blacks in more than 70 years. Then on Thursday evening came another culturally significant moment when Cardiff rolled out the red carpet to celebrate the first Welsh-language dub of the Star Wars franchise.
Stars of stage and screen who voiced the words of Luke Skywalker, Darth Vader, C-3PO et al in Welsh (Cymraeg) over the original 1977 Star Wars film took the plaudits at the Cineworld Cardiff screening.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Welsh can tell any story’: Cymraeg dub of Star Wars premieres in Cardiff

articles.author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
articles.description:
Surgeon at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary says he repeatedly voiced concerns and that patients may have died unnecessarily
A senior surgeon has called for a criminal investigation into a Scottish hospital after it emerged that at least 19 patients had died from avoidable complications due to surgery.
Dr Mohammed Habib, a consultant at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, said he had repeatedly reported concerns about the hospital’s liver and pancreatic surgery from 2021 onwards and believed dozens of patients may have died unnecessarily there.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Call for police to investigate Scottish hospital after 19 deaths due to surgery

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Reasons to refuse planning permission are limited to ‘public safety’ and ‘amenity’, writes James Ward
In response to your report (Rip out ugly clutter to help revive UK high streets, says thinktank, 13 November) perhaps we could start with the harbinger of high-street decline, the digital advertising screen. You know the ones, the pavement-blocking LED monoliths, with screens on both sides broadcasting six ads per minute to passersby.
Even as shops have shuttered, numbers of such ad machines skyrocketed 256% between 2018 and 2025. The ads shown are invariably for global mega-corporations, further driving commerce online, and for unhealthy products such as junk food, alcohol, gambling and vapes (although the latter are to be banned from 1 June 2027). At nearly 3 metres tall and 1.24 metres wide, they contribute to pavement clutter and disrupt sightlines of historic town centres.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Save our streets from yet more advertising | Letter

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Steven Morris
articles.description:
Joanne Young, who has waived anonymity, was subjected to years of drugging and rape by former Swindon councillor, who invited other men to assault her
When Philip Young served as a Conservative party councillor for Swindon council, his contemporaries viewed him as a perfectly normal family man with “no edge to him”.
But behind closed doors he orchestrated a systematic campaign of abuse against his then wife, Joanne Young, secretly administering sedatives to render her unconscious, disoriented and amnesiac. Over a period of at least 15 years, he and other men raped and sexually assaulted her in her own bed at their home in Swindon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spiked nightcaps and invitations to strangers: how Philip Young sexually abused his wife for 15 years

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Citizens Advice criticises company for failing to meet Ofcom requirements while reporting increased revenue
Royal Mail has been accused of offering a “pot luck service” to consumers as it looks likely to miss first-class delivery targets for the fourth consecutive year.
The postal service, whose parent company was bought for £3.6bn by the Czech billionaire Daniel Křetínský last year, is meant to deliver 90% of its first-class post by the next working day and 95% of second-class post within three working days according to targets set by the regulator, Ofcom.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Pot luck service’: Royal Mail on course to miss delivery targets for fourth year in a row

articles.author: Andrew Pulver
articles.description:
Westminster joins wave of ‘job-stealing’ memes after the actor’s late success edging out the other contenders to be the new 007
Everybody is trying to get a piece of the Bond action: even the UK government.
In a post on its official Instagram account, the UK government promoted its youth jobs guarantee scheme, first announced in August, with a picture of Robert Pattinson as Bond with the joke caption: “Robert Pattinson to apply for all 90,000 jobs created for young people through Youth Employment Scheme.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Robert Pattinson to apply for 90,000 more jobs? UK government trolls James Bond actor

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Modelling in draft of 10-year London plan threatens Sadiq Khan’s promises on improving air quality
Car use in London will rise by 10% over the next decade with cycling and walking falling as a proportion of trips, according to an official forecast by the city’s mayoralty, putting into doubt Sadiq Khan’s promises on air quality and the environment.
Based on projections in the draft version of the latest 10-year London plan, drawn up by the mayor’s office and Transport for London (TfL), road congestion from a growing population would slow buses down, while packed tube services might require stations to close regularly to ease numbers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Car use in London forecast to rise by 10% in next decade

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
Scientists use lightweight tracker to map wading bird’s extraordinary migration from Norfolk to the Arctic and back
A bar-tailed godwit called Phil has completed a 6,800-mile journey from Norfolk to Siberia and back again, in the first UK mapping of the endurance feats of this long-distance migrant.
A wading bird not much larger than a pigeon, the bar-tailed godwit is known for making the longest recorded non-stop migratory flight of any bird. Populations that visit Britain spend summers breeding in the Arctic Circle before retreating to the unfrozen wetlands of Britain in winter. In 2022, one bar-tailed godwit made the longest recorded non-stop flight, 13,560km over 11 days from Alaska to Tasmania.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Meet Phil, the bar-tailed godwit tracked on a 6,800-mile round trip to Siberia

articles.author: Presented by Annie Kelly with Jessica Elgot and David McAllister; produced by Eleanor Biggs, Alex Atack, Harriet Mogie and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
Deputy political editor Jessica Elgot and influential MEP David McAllister on the prospect of the UK rejoining the European Union, before Friday’s UK-EU summit
On Friday, Andy Burnham will be in Brussels, to sign off a series of new deals between the UK and the EU.
The prime minister claims the deals – covering areas from food to youth mobility to carbon emissions – will boost UK GDP by £17bn.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brejoin? Is Andy Burnham going to reverse Brexit? – podcast

articles.author: Sandra Laville Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Populations at lowest level on record with 45% of native breeding species in decline, environment watchdog says
The environment secretary, Angela Eagle, her ministers and Natural England are breaking the law by failing to intervene to slow the “deeply concerning” decline of Britain’s wild birds, the UK’s environment regulator has said.
