New data shows that wild bird populations have dropped to their lowest level on record, with almost half – 45% – of 132 native breeding species in decline over a five-year period.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK government ‘breaking the law’ by not stopping decline of wild birds

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Animal welfare charities criticise ‘backwards step’ on foie gras, production of which has been banned in UK since 2007
Ministers will drop plans to ban foie gras imports into the UK in order to smooth a trade deal with the EU that will be announced this week.
As first reported by the Financial Times, the proposed ban will be officially dropped on Friday when the government announces its sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) trade deal with the EU to reduce checks and paperwork on imports and exports of food and drink with the bloc.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ministers to drop foie gras imports ban to help seal EU food trade deal

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal; produced by George McDonagh, Ivor Manley , Harriet Mogie and Rudi Zygadlo; executive producer Eli Block
articles.description:
There are about a million young people across the country not in employment, education or training. Could Alan Milburn’s landmark report help change that? Richard Partington reports
The UK has one of the worst rates in Europe when it comes to youth unemployment. From the savage cuts to youth services during austerity, to the impacts of the pandemic and now the threat of AI to entry level jobs, young people across the country are feeling that the social contract is broken.
But now Alan Milburn, the 68-year-old New Labour veteran, has published a radical review urging the government to spend billions on a new deal for young people.

articles.title: Can Labour end the youth unemployment crisis? – podcast

Alan Milburn says his plan to get young people into work will save only £200m a year

UK politics live – latest updates

articles.title: Alan Milburn says 'Great British promise' to young people is being broken – video

articles.description:
It is a big week for Andy Burnham as two of his big policy priorities enter the spotlight. On Tuesday, the Milburn review of welfare for under-25s is published, which could ignite old Labour tensions over benefit cuts.
Then, later this week, Burnham will be in Brussels for the UK-EU summit to discuss a potential new deal. But, as Pippa has signalled, cabinet ministers have told Burnham to put the brake on some of the discussions to ensure the government is not out of step with the public.
Is it too little too late?
You can read Rowena Mason’s article on benefits for under-25s here.

articles.description:
Multiple women allege David Walliams abused his power and position as a celebrity to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were young women, an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News has found. He denies the allegations.

In a letter addressed to journalists working on this investigation, Walliams writes: 'Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

'I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.'

He adds: 'I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.'
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The allegations against David Walliams | Investigation by the Guardian and ITV News

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Residents of Astley in Greater Manchester will tell public inquiry next week of ‘cacophony’ of noise causing sleep deprivation and depression
When Stephen Retford retired from the police in 2006, he looked forward to a quiet life after nearly three decades catching villains. But now the former detective has landed another big case – one that is extremely close to home.
“It’s the total injustice of it,” the 70-year-old seethed, staring up at the 18-metre-high mega-warehouse that looms over the quiet village of Astley in Greater Manchester. Residents are up in arms about the “monster” construction, likening it to having a “cruise ship in our back garden”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s a feeling of being screwed over’: once-quiet village despairs over ‘monster’ warehouse

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
Scheme in Derry aims to sow confidence by getting people with learning and physical disabilities into wrestling
The music thumped, the lights blazed and from the ring the announcer did a countdown. “Who is ready to rumble?” he roared. The bellows and cheers indicated that the crowd at St Columb’s Hall in Derry on Saturday night was more than ready for the Foyle Rumble, and so began a wrestling extravaganza of heroes and villains in leotards, masks and kneepads.
The blend of athleticism and scripted storytelling would have been familiar to fans of WrestleMania, but this Northern Irish version came with a twist: many of the performers have learning or physical disabilities, and the characters they play in the ring do not quite stay in the ring.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No matter what, he doesn’t quit’: disabled wrestlers draw strength from ring alter egos

articles.author: Chris Osuh, Aamna Mohdin and Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Some relatives of British citizens say they feel left behind, but announcement has brought relief to many care workers
“The only time we’re regarded as human beings is when they need a lot of hands onboard, like during Covid. But after that, we’re tossed away like we’re some rubbish,” Aneisha Williams says.
Williams, 39, was months from qualifying for indefinite leave to remain after 10 years in the UK. But claiming housing benefit could delay her settlement for years under Shabana Mahmood’s “earned settlement” plans.

articles.title: ‘I feel free now’: Shabana Mahmood’s immigration shake-up provokes mixed emotions

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time
Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games has announced, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.
The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar said also it had sold 32.5m units of the game on prerelease, setting a record across platforms.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A new record for entertainment’: Grand Theft Auto VI sales hit $3.8bn on first day of release, developer says

articles.author: Lauren Almeida and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout

Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.
Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.

articles.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading

articles.author: Lauren Gould
articles.description:
Our favorite screen alternatives, including guided watercolor books, jigsaw puzzles and a Mexican cookbook

The best holiday gifts – obsessively tested

Logging off is en vogue. From touting analog bags to playing vinyl records, many of us are tired of living life behind a screen.
So 2026 may be the ideal year to gift some low-tech entertainment instead of the newest iPhone. These days, we’re all trying to connect with the “real world” more, and the latest string of tech outages has been a good nudge to buy stuff that won’t glitch.
Visit our ultimate holiday gift guide for obsessively vetted gift ideas, or get inspired by our full array of guides, including a gift guide for the person who has everything and a guide to cozy gifts.

articles.title: We’ve tried everything to get off our phones. These 11 things work (and make great gifts)

articles.author: Maya Yang and Alfie Packham
articles.description:
Rockstar’s newest installment of its hit franchise still has plenty of action, along with a dose of ‘healthy masculinity’
Described as the biggest entertainment launch in history, the new Grand Theft Auto game has prompted avid fans around the world to take the day off work, stock up on snacks and celebrate its arrival after 13 years of waiting.
While some have already spent hours immersed in the game’s criminal escapades, others have found themselves doing household chores, building houses or simply taking in the scenery – which includes more than 170 flora and fauna species native to Florida. GTA VI has generated extraordinary global anticipation for its action-packed gameplay, but players are now finding new delight in the game’s more intimate moments.

articles.title: ‘The greatest game ever made’: readers and Guardian staff on Grand Theft Auto VI

Fed up with condensation, mould and musty smells? A dehumidifier could help – plus, they’re a cheaper way to dry laundry compared with tumble dryers
• The best electric blankets and heated throws, tested by our expert
You don’t have to live in the American deep south to feel the effects of humidity. At home, just breathing makes the air more humid, let alone cooking or showering.
And when it gets too humid, it’s bad for our health as well as our homes. In fact, the two are connected: humidity lets mould and dust mites flourish – and they, in turn, can trigger asthma and allergies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The best dehumidifiers: 14 favourites to beat damp and cut bills, tested

articles.author: Sarah Matthews
articles.description:
They claim to reduce fine lines, blemishes and redness – but which stand up to scrutiny? After consulting dermatologists and putting them to the test, we have crowned a brand new number one
• The best anti-ageing creams, serums and treatments
LED face masks are booming in popularity – despite being one of the most expensive at-home beauty products to hit the market. They claim to reduce the appearance of fine lines, stop spots and calm redness, with some even combining different types of light to enhance the benefits.
However, it’s wise to be sceptical about new treatments that are costly and non-invasive, and to do your research before you buy. With this in mind, I interviewed doctors and dermatologists to find out whether these light therapy devices work.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Light therapy without remortgaging the house’: the best LED face masks – tested

articles.author: Henrietta Moore
articles.description:
It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers
AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI.
Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. Economists coined a term for this in recent years: brain capital.
Professor Dame Henrietta Moore is founder and director of the UCL Institute for Global Prosperity and co-leads The New Alignment, the institute’s G20 policy programme
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI is imposing a hidden ‘cognitive tax’ on the lowest-paid workers

articles.author: Garrison Lovely
articles.description:
Frontier models can exploit software flaws faster than the world can fix them. And the risks extend far beyond the cyber realm
You’re not crazy to feel the world is coming apart at the seams.
Within the last week, outages took down core services at Microsoft, United Airlines and JPMorgan Chase. On Friday, all US domestic departures were grounded for the second time since 9/11. And on Tuesday, CNN reported the NSA’s highly classified internal communications network went down. In each case, officials or the companies said there was no evidence of a cyber-attack.

articles.title: Will AI break the internet? | Garrison Lovely

articles.author: Victoria Turk
articles.description:
Our tech expert and new mum tested 17 monitors for picture quality, battery life and reliability – here’s what she recommends
• The best eco-friendly baby products
Moving my baby into her own room to sleep felt liberating and stressful. She was ready for her own space – but was I ready to let her out of my sight? Well, the first thing I did was buy a video baby monitor, so clearly I wasn’t. But it meant she could sleep peacefully in her new room and I could sneak a reassuring peek from afar whenever I felt the need.
There’s a huge range of baby monitors, from simple audio-only options to sophisticated video models. Some even include wearables or other devices to track a baby’s breathing or heart rate, while others offer AI features to analyse sleep patterns. At their most basic, baby monitors typically consist of a baby unit, which you position near the baby, and a parent unit, which lets you hear and/or see them. With video models, the baby unit is essentially a camera, while the parent unit is a screen. Many are also wifi-enabled, meaning you can connect the monitor to your smartphone and view the live feed through an app instead of using a dedicated parent unit (read on for security advice).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: I’m a tech expert and new mum. Here’s what I learned testing 17 baby monitors

State attorney says scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if company misled investors
California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.
Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based company’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.

articles.title: California investigates Nvidia over whether chip exports ended up in China

articles.author: Alexis Petridis
articles.description:
From sampling to streaming, the rock legend has always been in thrall to technology – but is superintelligence a step too far? Back with an epic new album, he unpacks his remarkable ideas
Peter Gabriel asks me to fetch my laptop: he wants to show me a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with a bonobo called Kanzi. In fairness, said footage is, as Gabriel suggests, “extraordinary”. Working with primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, who developed a means of communicating with bonobos involving sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard, Gabriel plays droning chords on a synthesiser while Kanzi picks out complementary notes on a piano. “Look, she likes that note, which is a ninth, and then she finds the octave,” he enthuses as the video plays. “There’s a real musicality there.”
It is all deeply unlikely, but it seems the perfect illustration of how easily a conversation with Gabriel can go wildly – if fascinatingly – off-piste. I’ve only been in his company for 10 minutes, long enough to ask a solitary question about his epic new album o\i: its 13 tracks last nearly 90 minutes, the result, he suggests, of a longstanding interest in African music “which made me realise that a song could last as long as a song could last”, and of “being old enough to think ‘fuck it’, really”. For anyone who feels that an hour and a half of exquisitely arranged, beautifully produced, occasionally deeply strange art rock – its sound shapeshifting from the folk-flecked A Hard Lesson to the glowing pop hues of Till Your Mind Is Shining – is too meagre an offering, it arrives in two versions: a “dark” mix by US producer Tchad Blake and a “bright” version that’s the handiwork of Mike “Spike” Stent, famed for working with everyone from U2 and Madonna to Frank Ocean and Harry Styles.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We’re the most arrogant of all apes!’ A delightfully mind-expanding encounter with Peter Gabriel

AI startup and Claude chatbot maker became one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded businesses with final share price of $97

Anthropic’s historic stock market debut: key takeaways, and what comes next for the AI industry 

Anthropic closed its first day of trading on the US stock market about 17% higher than its initial public offering price. At the close of market on Thursday, Anthropic shares were trading at just over $97 with a nearly $1.3tn total market capitalization, $1.75tn fully diluted.

Nonetheless, Anthropic’s ranked among the biggest stock market flotations in history. The artificial intelligence startup, founded in 2021, became one of the most valuable publicly traded businesses in the world.

Anti-AI groups gather in front of Nasdaq exchange in Times Square and Anthropic’s headquarters in San Francisco
As the artificial intelligence startup Anthropic debuted on the US stock market at an eye-popping $2tn valuation on Thursday, protesters from anti-AI groups rallied in front of the Nasdaq exchange at its New York City headquarters in Times Square and several were arrested. articles.author: Keza MacDonald
articles.description:
Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids

Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI?

I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “no way”. Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me. She was genuinely shocked to learn that an 18-rating on a video game was a flag for adult content, rather than an indication of its difficulty.
Grand Theft Auto VI is released this week. It is an incredible creative and technical feat, conjuring a realistic-looking and exhaustively detailed virtual Florida filled with every kind of filth and criminality you could imagine. It is brilliant, entertainingly observed and even sometimes unexpectedly touching, largely thanks to a central love story between the player couple, Jason and Lucia. It is lewd, violent and frequently hilarious. It is also absolutely full of stuff that I really would not want my 10 and seven-year-old boys to see or hear. I have never played a game that has more thoroughly earned its 18 rating.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child

articles.author: Keza MacDonald
articles.description:
There’s a vast amount to absorb in Leonida, but these pointers will rev up your criminal engines and allow you to better enjoy the ride

Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI?

Leonida is so huge as to be overwhelming and in the opening hours, the game bombards you with tonnes of info that you will inevitably forget. But I’ve done nothing but play this game for weeks and I’m here to help. Here’s what I wished I’d known at the start
Walk faster. I found that Jason and Lucia walk incredibly slowly. If you go into the options menu, you can select “fast walk” as the default walking speed, which sped them up just a little without ruining the pace or atmosphere of the game.
